limitations: Single-process, in-memory cache lookups only; no DB, network, or full governance path is exercised.
No CPU isolation, affinity, priority, frequency, or GC policy changes were applied.
Only governance_cache.py and core.asyncio_compat.py are loaded directly; no backend/core/__init__.py or app startup is executed.
No pyperf dependency; time.perf_counter_ns with manual repetitions is used.
Timer resolution and two-call timer overhead are reported separately and are not subtracted.
Other host processes may add noise; no soak or CPU-isolation claim is made.
Seeded policy-shaped fixtures are not real governance decisions.
TTL uses the cache's wall-clock implementation; a run that reaches the TTL fails instead of reporting.
Results are machine/run specific and do not grant universal throughput or PERF-01 qualification.

nonqualification.statement: This bounded cache microbenchmark does not qualify database, current-authority, budget, approval, Oracle, HTTP/API, cold-start, or full-governance latency.

scope.cache_instances: one fresh in-process GovernanceCache per measured scope
scope.seeded_values: in-memory benchmark fixtures, not real governance decisions
scope.timed_operation_notes: Returned values and cache statistics are validated outside each timed read; per-lookup latency samples validate the returned value after the stop timestamp.

timer.overhead_method: two consecutive time.perf_counter_ns() calls; loop overhead is included
